name: The large dwelling-house on lot 7 of block 16

documented_range.note: A BUILDING ON THIS LOT IS DOCUMENTED; THIS BUILDING IS NOT. G. Spring's notice — "LOT No. 7, in block No. 16, one lot east of Haddock's Tavern, on Lake street … There is on said lot a large Dwelling-House and fine well" — ran 6 printings, 1834-06-18 to 1834-11-19 (chicago_democrat_1834_06_18#c006, chicago_democrat_1834_07_02#c053, chicago_democrat_1834_07_09#c024, chicago_democrat_1834_09_03#c005, chicago_democrat_1834_10_15#c006, chicago_democrat_1834_11_19#c010). Six settings of one notice, dated June 18 1834 and standing to November. Four read the neighbour as Haddock's Tavern and are legible end to end; the setting of 1834-07-09 reads Maddock's, which data/research/newspapers/identity.json merges into Haddock's on those four; the setting of 1834-07-02 is damaged at both the tavern's name and the building's and its own claim refused to supply either word. THE ADDRESS RESOLVES THROUGH THE PLAT: block No. 16 is blk_south_water_dearborn (`inferred`, counted along the tier from a numeral read off Wright's 1834 sheet — data/traces/thompson_block_numbering.json), and lot No. 7 is the third lot east of the Dearborn corner under a lot scheme graded `conjectural` because no sheet drew the lines it numbers. This roof is the one standing on that lot. THE GRADE IS THE WEAKEST LINK IN THAT CHAIN and not the notice's own; docs/RESEARCH/thompson_block_numbering.md §§ 6-7 is the reading, and § 6 is the three independent statements that agree on this block. The last printing is 1834-11-19, seven and a half months before the scene date. That the house still stood on 1835-07-01 is INFERRED and not documented: a dwelling advertised for sale over five months is a standing building rather than a project, nothing in the corpus records a fire, a removal or a rebuilding on this lot, and the town of 1835 was adding houses rather than losing them. What would replace the inference is a printing of 1835 that names the lot; the register holds none.

position.symbolic_location: Lot 7 of block 16 — the north side of Lake Street, the third lot east of Dearborn, in the South Division block bounded by South Water, State, Lake and Dearborn
position.note: Interpretive placement on a GENERATED lot, not a recovered parcel. The lot geometry is the K7 plat module's — this project has never read Thompson's numbering off a sheet, and the side lot lines and the alley are conjectural even where the block face is not. The building stands 5.5 m back from its street edge, which is a typology for the period and not a measurement of this lot. The whole footprint — not its centre — is tested against the platted street corridors, against its own lot lines and against every other footprint in the dataset, so no invented building of this parcel stands in the roadway; clearing the roadway is not the same as standing on a recovered lot.

derivation.reason: The lot is numbered and the address resolves onto it, but no source states where on the lot the house stood, how big it was or which way it faced. The position inside the lot is the 665-roof programme's typology, exactly as it was before the address was read.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 6 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn from the set on this record's stable key, then advanced so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

occupants.note: ADOPTED BY THE INFERRED-HOUSEHOLD PROGRAMME (docs/ROADMAP.md K1, phase two). This anonymous roof is the dwelling of an inferred carpenter's household (17 of 20 this layer infers): hh_inf_carpenter_south_17 in data/residents/households/. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit. The occupant is hypothesised from the town's demonstrable needs - the 1835 census of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings against the trades Andreas's 1833 roster names - and is not a person: no name is claimed and no figure is drawn.

research_note: THE ADDRESS IS DOCUMENTED AND THE FABRIC UNDER IT IS NOT. This roof was raised by the 665-roof programme as an anonymous count-unit and is unchanged by the adoption — its existence as drawn, its position inside the lot, its footprint, its family and its form are all still invented, and it still counts once toward the programme. What changed is that the lot it stands on is named by a period notice, so the card says whose house this ground carried instead of naming nobody. THE NOTICE SAYS `LARGE` AND THE ROOF UNDER IT IS THE BLOCK'S SMALLEST FAMILY — a D3 one-room frame cottage of 5.36 x 6.38 m. The address is documented and the fabric is not, so the mismatch is a statement about the reconstruction and not about the evidence; correcting it means re-dealing the block's family mix and re-baking, which is a second demonstration and is filed as its own ticket. THE WELL: The notice attests a well ON THE LOT and gives it no position, no diameter, no curb and no cover, so the whole of a drawn well would be invention standing beside a documented building — and this project draws small ground objects from a RULE that a gate re-derives (the yard goods, the dooryard pickets, the lot-line fences), not from one hand-placed record. There is no well layer to add a row to and writing one is more than this adoption. Filed as its own ticket rather than left as a silence. RECONSTRUCTED / GENERATED, NOT AN ATTESTED NAMED BUILDING. The block, its scheduled roof count and its family mix follow the 665-roof programme; exact presence, lot, position, footprint, finish and instance-level form are interpretive.
